# Establishment log — bardo-thodol-013 (pp. 115–121), 2026-11-23

The last part of text **ga**, and of the run. It starts at 115.5 with the call on the lama (ཁྱོད་རང་གི་བླ་མའི་…) and goes on to
the verse prayer of the bardo (ཀྱཻ་མ་བག་ཆགས་དྲག་པོས་…, 116.2–118.1). After that it says how often to say the prayer, gives the
benefits of the Thos grol, and ends with the instruction to read it aloud. The colophon follows: Karma Gling pa's discovery, the line of
transmission, and the scribe གྷ་གྷ་དྷརྨ་པ་མུ་དྲ. Text ga ends on 121.5 with …གུས་པར་ཞུསོ།. The rest of that line is blank, apart
from one ༔ standing alone against the right frame. No other text begins on p. 121, and no sentence runs over to p. 122.

There is no transcription of this print for ga. Three readers read the images line by line from scratch. All three ran on the strongest model,
and no Sonnet role ran. Each had the other recension (readings/witness_ga.txt) open as a guide only.
- Reader A read 115.5 (from ཁྱོད) through p. 117.
- Reader B read pp. 118–119.
- Reader C read pp. 120–121.

The full tables are in readings/read_A-log.md, read_B-log.md and read_C-log.md. Every page has five lines. pp. 117, 119 and 121 are leaf fronts
and open with ༄༅༔ ༔.

**Seams.** Both are clean.
- 117.5/118.1 is …འབྱུང་ལྔའི་ཁམས་|རྣམས.
- 119.5/120.1 is …དེད་ནས་བྱུང|ཡང་འདིའི, with no tsheg.
- Reader B could not read one stack at 117.5. Reader A read it at full size as ཆཱར, with a small འ set under the ཆ. The fix writes it འཆར, which is also what the other recension has.

## Kept, note only
- **117.1 དངངས་སྐྲག་བར་དོའི་འཇིགས་ང[?]་མི་འབྱུང་ཤོག.** ང is not a word here, and the line wants a syllable such as སྣང (as in 116.3 འཇིགས་སྣང) or པ (the other recension). This is a guess, so it is not corrected. The note should give both candidates and the sense "may the terrors … not arise".
- **116.1 ཐུགས་རྗེས་མ་བཏང་ཞིག[?]་གྱིས་ལ.** The other recension has མ་གཏང་གྱིས་ལ. The sense is "do not let go of [me] with your compassion" either way.
- **120.2 ད་ལྟ་ལན་ཅིག** "now, once", where the other recension has དེ་ལྟར་ལན་གཅིག. It reads as printed: "even if one hears it once now and does not understand".

- **121.4 …འདྲ་བའི་གནས་ནས** "from the place", where the other recension has གཏེར་ནས "from the treasure". Keep.
- 121.4–5: the line of transmission has དེའི་ where the other recension has དེས་, adds རིམ་པར་, and gives the guru's name as སུ་རྱ་ཙནྡྲ, without རསྨི. The scribe is spelled གྷ་གྷ་. The print has no closing dedication (the other recension's འདི་བྲིས་དགེ་བས…).
